meta: /blogs/hair-care/is-good-circulation-important-for-healthy-hair-growth

Scalp circulation supplies oxygen and nutrients to growing hair, and the article says studies have found lower oxygen and blood flow in thinning scalps. It also notes that many hair researchers believe there is ample blood flow in all scalps.
/blogs/hair-care/dandruff-cause-hair-thinning

Mild dandruff, which causes flakes and itchiness, does not on its own lead to hair thinning or hair loss. The article says inflammation from conditions such as seborrheic dermatitis, and heavy scratching, can contribute to hair loss.
/blogs/hair-care/7-daily-habits-that-damage-hair

The article lists seven daily habits that damage hair, beginning with products that contain parabens, benzoates, phthalates, SLS and artificial fragrances. It says increased shedding in the shower or on the pillow is what prompts many people to look for causes.
/blogs/hair-care/b-vitamins-hair-growth

The B vitamins are a group of eight nutrients that support red blood cells, energy levels and brain function. The article names biotin, folate (B9) and B12 as the three most important B vitamins for hair.
/blogs/hair-care/castor-oil-for-hair-growth
Castor oil is a vegetable oil from the seeds of the Ricinus communis plant and is made up mostly of ricinoleic acid. The article covers its use for hair, skin and lashes, and its side effects.
/blogs/hair-care/lavender-oil-for-hair

Lavender oil is an essential oil extracted from lavender flowers by steam distillation. The article covers its use in hair care, how to dilute and apply it, and possible side effects such as skin sensitivity.
/blogs/hair-care/dextran

Dextran is a complex carbohydrate made of glucose chains, produced by bacteria or yeast fermenting sucrose. The article says it is water-soluble with a high molecular weight and discusses its use in hair care.
/blogs/hair-care/shrinkage

Shrinkage is the reduction in hair length that happens when curly, coily or kinky hair dries or is manipulated. The article explains that wet hair stretches and appears longer, then retracts as it dries.
/blogs/hair-care/fade

A fade, as the article uses the term, is a coloring technique that gradually blends hair from darker roots to lighter ends. The article says this creates a seamless transition that makes gray hair and root growth less noticeable.
/blogs/hair-care/schisandra

Schisandra chinensis is a fruit-bearing vine native to parts of Asia, also called wu wei zi or the five-flavored berry. The article says it has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine as an adaptogen to help the body handle stress.
/blogs/hair-care/fully-vital-reviews-dani

This is a first-person review by a health coach who developed hair thinning on a ketogenic diet and with polycystic ovary syndrome. She describes using a three-month hair system daily, and the page includes before and after photos.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-breakage

Hair breakage is when hair strands snap or fracture along the shaft, leaving shorter, weaker hair. The article says it differs from hair loss, which is shedding from the scalp, and can show up as split ends, frizz or brittle texture.
/blogs/hair-care/butylene-glycol

Butylene glycol is a clear, odorless, water-soluble organic compound from the glycol family. The article explains that it is used in cosmetic and hair care products as a solvent, humectant and conditioning agent.
/blogs/hair-care/citric-acid
Citric acid is a compound found in citrus fruits that also plays a role in the body's energy production. The article covers its use in hair care to adjust pH and exfoliate the scalp.
/blogs/hair-care/derma-roller-for-hair

A derma roller, also called a microneedle roller, is a handheld device with hundreds of tiny needles that create micro-injuries on the skin. The article says it was designed for skincare and is now used in hair care.
/blogs/hair-care/derma-roller-for-beard

A derma roller, also called a microneedle roller, is a handheld device with hundreds of tiny needles that create microscopic punctures in the skin. The article explains how it is used on the beard and that it is also used in skincare for scars and wrinkles.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-botox-treatment
Hair botox is a cosmetic procedure used on hair damaged by heat styling, chemicals and the environment. The article notes it does not involve injecting toxins and compares it with keratin smoothing.
/blogs/hair-care/derma-roller-for-hair-loss

A derma roller, also called a microneedling roller, is a handheld device with hundreds of tiny needles that create micro-injuries on the scalp. The article says the needles range from 0.25 mm to 1.5 mm.
/blogs/hair-care/panthenol

Panthenol, also called provitamin B5, is a water-soluble ingredient derived from pantothenic acid and used in hair care products. The article says it helps hair retain moisture and adds shine and elasticity.
/blogs/hair-care/emollient

Emollients are ingredients that moisturize and soften the hair and scalp and are found in shampoos, conditioners and leave-in products. The article says they help restore moisture and hydration in hair.
/blogs/hair-care/is-dimethicone-bad-for-hair

Dimethicone is a silicone-based polymer used in hair and skin products to smooth the surface and lock in moisture. The article says it can build up on hair and scalp over time and lists lighter alternatives.
/blogs/hair-care/how-much-hair-is-normal-to-lose-in-the-shower

Losing around 50 to 100 hairs a day is considered normal, and some of that shedding is seen in the shower. The article explains that hair type, length and washing frequency affect how much you notice, and when to see a professional.
/blogs/hair-care/keratin

Keratin is a fibrous structural protein that serves as a main building block of hair, skin and nails. The article explains that it is naturally present in hair and plays a role in the strength and resilience of each strand.
/blogs/hair-care/is-salt-water-good-for-your-hair
Salt water can add texture and volume, but it can also leave hair dry and brittle. The article lists these pros and cons and gives tips for protecting hair before and after swimming.
/blogs/hair-care/female-pattern-baldness

Female pattern baldness is a common hair loss disorder caused by genetic, hormonal and other factors. The article says it can affect over 50 percent of women over 50, according to the American Hair Loss Association, and lists approaches to managing it.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-thinning

Hair thinning is a noticeable reduction in hair volume and thickness and can happen gradually or suddenly. The article says it often results from genetics, hormonal imbalances, nutritional deficiencies and lifestyle choices.
/blogs/hair-care/vitamin-d3

Vitamin D3, also known as cholecalciferol, is a form of vitamin D made in the skin with sunlight or obtained from food and supplements. The article discusses its role in overall health and hair growth.
/blogs/hair-care/folate

Folate, also known as vitamin B9, is a water-soluble nutrient the body cannot produce, so it must come from food or supplements. The article lists sources such as leafy greens, legumes, citrus, avocados and fortified cereals.
/blogs/hair-care/bed-head

Bed head is the messy, tousled hair some people wake up with after sleeping. The article describes how to get and manage the look, including wetting the hair, using a leave-in conditioner and finger combing.
/blogs/hair-care/finasteride

Finasteride is an FDA-approved medication primarily used for hair loss in men. The article says it belongs to the 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors, which inhibit the conversion of testosterone into DHT, and discusses its use in women.
/blogs/hair-care/dermatologist

A dermatologist is a medical professional who specializes in diagnosing skin, hair and nail conditions. The article says a dermatologist can identify underlying issues, such as genetics, hormonal imbalances, stress or diet, that affect hair growth.
/blogs/hair-care/synthetic-hair
Synthetic hair refers to man-made hair extensions or wigs created from synthetic fibers designed to resemble the texture and feel of natural hair. The article covers its benefits and alternatives.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-replacement

Hair replacement covers surgical and non-surgical procedures that restore hair in areas where thinning or balding has occurred. The article describes the methods, their benefits and downsides, and alternatives, with the aim of a natural-looking result.
/blogs/hair-care/anagen-phase

The anagen phase is the active growth stage of the hair cycle, when follicles are producing new hair strands. The article says cells in the hair bulb divide rapidly during this phase, which helps determine hair length and thickness.
/blogs/hair-care/thyroid-hair-loss
The thyroid gland regulates metabolism and energy, and its hormones T3 and T4 play a role in the hair growth cycle. The article explains how a thyroid imbalance can be connected to hair loss.
/blogs/hair-care/biotin-vs-collagen
Biotin, also called vitamin B7, supports healthy hair, skin and nails, while collagen is a structural protein. The article compares the two supplements and their roles in hair growth, skin and nails.
/blogs/hair-care/bimatoprost

Bimatoprost is a synthetic prostamide originally recognized for its use in ophthalmology, or eye care. The article discusses its journey into hair growth and says it is known for acting on hair follicles, potentially affecting hair density and length.
/blogs/hair-care/androgenetic-alopecia

Androgenetic alopecia, commonly known as female pattern baldness, is a hereditary hair loss condition in women. The article says it is characterized by gradual thinning and a widening part, and arises from genetic factors and the influence of androgens.
/blogs/hair-care/low-level-laser-therapy
Low level laser therapy, also called red light or cold laser therapy, uses low-level lasers or LEDs on the scalp. The article describes how it works, its benefits and downsides, and alternatives.
/blogs/hair-care/trichoscopy

Trichoscopy, also called scalp dermoscopy, is a non-invasive procedure that uses a handheld device called a trichoscope to examine the scalp and hair. The article says it magnifies the scalp up to 200 times to show details not visible to the naked eye.
/blogs/hair-care/formaldehyde

Formaldehyde is a naturally occurring organic compound made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen that is widely used across industries. The article discusses its role in hair products, though the page's claims about it are not supported.
/blogs/hair-care/stem-cell-therapy

Stem cell therapy uses stem cells, the body's building blocks that can become various cell types, in an effort to rejuvenate hair follicles. The article describes how the technique is used in the context of hair growth.
/blogs/hair-care/anti-dandruff-shampoo

Anti-dandruff shampoo is a hair care product formulated to address dandruff, a common scalp condition with flakiness and itching. The article says these shampoos contain active ingredients designed to target the causes of dandruff.
/blogs/hair-care/hydrolyzed-protein
Hydrolyzed protein is protein that has been broken down into smaller molecules, which makes it easier for hair to absorb. The article explains why it is a popular hair care ingredient.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-cloning

Hair cloning is an experimental approach in hair restoration that takes a small sample of follicles, multiplies the cells in a laboratory and implants them back in the scalp. The article describes the process, its stated benefits and its downsides.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-elastics

Hair elastics, also called hair ties or hair bands, are small accessories made of rubber, silicone or fabric that secure hair in ponytails, buns and braids. The article covers how they work, their benefits, potential downsides and alternatives.
/blogs/hair-care/best-hair-growth-serum-for-blondes

Hair serums can suit light-colored hair, but the article says people with oily or fine hair should use them sparingly or choose lightweight formulas. It lists factors to consider when picking a serum for blonde hair.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-volumizer

A hair volumizer is a styling product that adds volume and thickness to hair and comes as sprays, mousses and serums. The article says these products coat the hair shaft and lift it at the roots to create fuller-looking hair.
/blogs/hair-care/best-hair-growth-serum-for-black-hair

The article reviews hair growth serums for Black hair and says to look for key ingredients such as biotin, also known as vitamin B7. It describes common hair concerns and how a serum can fit a routine.
/blogs/hair-care/best-hair-growth-serum-for-vibrant-hair
The article says red hair dyes often fade quickly and that vibrant color needs extra care. It reviews hair serums for colored hair and explains what they are formulated to do.
/blogs/hair-care/vegamour-vs-fully-vital

The article compares two vegan hair growth brands on shelf life, performance in humidity, eco-friendliness, ingredient quality, product range and price. It notes that the serums differ in size, at 30 ml and 55 ml.
/blogs/hair-care/viviscal-vs-fully-vital

The article compares two hair growth brands on safety and allergy considerations, short and long-term results, environmental concerns, required quantity per use and availability. It stresses that the path to fuller hair is a marathon, not a sprint.
/blogs/hair-care/organic-hair-serum

Organic hair serums use plant-based ingredients to nourish and protect the hair. The article advises choosing one by considering your hair type, your specific hair concerns and the results you want, and lists five serums.
/blogs/hair-care/catagen-phase

The catagen phase is the short transitional stage of the hair growth cycle that follows anagen, the growth phase, and comes before telogen, the resting phase. The article says follicles cease producing new hair strands and enter a brief dormancy.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-mineral-analysis

Hair mineral analysis is a test that measures the mineral content of a hair sample, such as iron, zinc, copper and magnesium. The article says the results can offer insight into nutrient imbalances that may affect hair.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-weaving

Hair weaving is an extension technique that adds length and volume by sewing in, bonding or clipping hair extensions to your natural hair. The article covers how it works, its benefits, its downsides such as expense and maintenance, and alternatives.
/blogs/hair-care/nutrafol-vs-fully-vital

The article compares two hair growth supplement brands on ingredients, safety, suitability for hair types and how long results take. It concludes the choice mostly comes down to personal preference and individual needs.
/blogs/hair-care/spoiled-child-hair-vs-fully-vital
The hair life cycle has three phases: anagen, the growth phase; catagen, the transition phase; and telogen, the resting phase. The article uses that cycle to compare two hair growth brands.
/blogs/hair-care/keratolytic-agents

Keratolytic agents are ingredients that soften the keratin protein holding dead skin cells together so they can shed more easily. The article says they are found in some hair products to exfoliate the scalp.
/blogs/hair-care/essential-fatty-acids

Essential fatty acids, or EFAs, are polyunsaturated fats the body needs but cannot produce on its own. The article explains the two primary types and why they matter for overall health and hair growth.
/blogs/hair-care/ingrown-hairs

An ingrown hair occurs when a hair curls back or grows sideways into the skin instead of growing out of the follicle. The article says it can cause red, inflamed bumps and happens when follicles become clogged.
/blogs/hair-care/mature-hairline

A mature hairline is the natural shift of the hairline slightly higher as people age, and it occurs in both men and women. The article lists its signs, such as slight, symmetrical recession without heavy shedding, and when to seek professional advice.
/blogs/hair-care/early-receding-hairline

An early receding hairline is a condition in which hair begins to thin and recede at the front of the scalp earlier than expected. The article says it can lead to a higher forehead and lower hair density in that area.
/blogs/hair-care/low-hairlines

A low hairline is a hairline that starts unusually low on the forehead, giving a smaller forehead area. The article covers how it occurs, whether it is hereditary and when the hairline typically starts thinning.
/blogs/hair-care/ugly-hairlines

An uneven or receding hairline is one that looks imbalanced or lacks fullness, and it affects both men and women. The article covers factors behind it and ways people approach it, including scalp care, diet and massage.
/blogs/hair-care/creatine-hair-loss

Scientific studies have not definitively shown a direct link between creatine supplements and hair loss. The article says some people may be more sensitive because of genetics and discusses other factors such as hormones, stress and overall health.
/blogs/hair-care/pura-dor-vs-fully-vital

The article compares two hair growth brands on safety and ingredients, including biotin, keratin, saw palmetto and niacin. It explains why knowing the ingredients helps you pick the product that suits you.
/blogs/hair-care/inflamed-hair-follicles

Inflamed hair follicles, also known as folliculitis, occur when hair follicles become irritated or infected. The article says they can cause redness, swelling and discomfort on the scalp, face or body, and sometimes hair loss in severe cases.
/blogs/hair-care/fully-vital-vs-thrive
Hair growth serums are products formulated to improve the condition of hair and scalp for people with thinning or who want thicker hair. The article compares two serum brands to help you choose.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-damage

Hair damage comes from heat styling, chemical treatments and environmental stress that affect the cuticle and inner shaft. The article says heat can strip moisture, causing dryness, split ends and breakage.
/blogs/hair-care/the-root-cause-of-scalp-inflammation-understanding-the-triggers-and-treatment-options

Scalp inflammation often shows up as an itchy, flaky or uncomfortable scalp. The article names harsh hair products, poor diet, stress, allergies and skin conditions such as psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis among the causes.
/blogs/hair-care/shedavi-or-fully-vital

Hair vitamins are supplements designed to provide the nutrients hair needs to grow stronger and healthier. The article compares two hair vitamin brands on approach, key active ingredients, how each works and safety.
/blogs/hair-care/vital-proteins-or-fully-vital

The article compares two hair vitamin brands and explains what ingredients to look for when choosing hair vitamins. It also stresses considering safety and potential side effects before you start taking any supplement.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-texture-chart

A hair texture chart is a tool for identifying your hair type, from straight to coily, along with details like strand thickness and moisture retention. The article explains how to use it to tailor your hair care and styling routine.
/blogs/hair-care/head-massage

A head massage stimulates the skin and hair follicles and increases blood flow to the scalp. The article also says it releases endorphins and oxytocin, which are linked to feelings of calm, and describes techniques and relaxation tips.
/blogs/hair-care/dead-hair

Hair is not alive like skin, so dead hair refers to strands that look dull and lifeless because of damage. The article says heat styling, coloring and sun exposure harm the cuticle, leaving hair weak and brittle.
/blogs/hair-care/does-wearing-a-hat-cause-hair-loss

Wearing a hat does not directly cause hair loss, according to the article. It says hair loss is mostly influenced by internal factors such as genetics and hormonal changes, though a very tight hat worn for a long time may cause temporary breakage.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-texture-types

Hair texture describes how your hair feels and looks, based on the thickness of individual strands and the overall pattern, such as straight, wavy or curly. The article is a guide to the different hair texture types.
/blogs/hair-care/hair-structure
Each hair has a root, a shaft and a tip, and the shaft is made of three layers: the cuticle, cortex and medulla. The article explains the role of each layer and how hair grows from the follicle.
/blogs/hair-care/certified-trichologist

Trichology is the branch of dermatology concerned with the health and disorders of the hair and scalp. The article says a trichologist specializes in hair loss, hair shaft problems and scalp conditions.
/blogs/hair-care/scalp-massage

Scalp massage works by mechanically stimulating blood vessels to dilate, which increases blood flow to the scalp and hair follicles. The article gives five reasons it is helpful for scalp and hair health.
/blogs/hair-care/how-to-thicken-hair

The article says the first step in thickening hair at home is to assess the current state of your hair and recognize the signs of thinning. It then covers nutrition, gentle hair care, scalp health and the hair growth cycle.
/blogs/hair-care/protein-overload-hair

Protein overload happens when too much protein builds up on the hair, leaving strands stiff, brittle and lifeless. The article lists causes and symptoms and recommends adjusting the hair care routine to balance moisture and protein.
/blogs/hair-care/dark-strawberry-blonde-hair

Dark strawberry blonde is a hair color that combines the light-catching qualities of blonde with the warmth of red. The article describes its deep, warm undertones and gives color and maintenance tips.
/blogs/hair-care/finasteride-results-timeline

Finasteride is an FDA-approved prescription medication used for androgenetic alopecia, also called male pattern baldness. The article explains that it blocks the enzyme that converts testosterone to DHT and describes the timeline of results and how people track progress.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/collagen

Collagen is a protein made of amino acids with a triple-helix structure that supports tissues in the body, including hair. The article says collagen surrounds each follicle and discusses its connection to hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/omega-3-fatty-acids
Omega-3 fatty acids are essential fats you must get from your diet because the body cannot make them. The article describes three main types, ALA, EPA and DHA, and their role in hair health.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/cysteine-complexes

Cysteine complexes are formulations designed to deliver the amino acid cysteine to the hair to reinforce its strength. The article notes that cysteine is especially abundant in keratin, the main protein in hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/riboflavin-for-radiance

Riboflavin, also called vitamin B2, is a water-soluble vitamin essential for energy production and cell function. The article says it also helps the body make amino acids and fatty acids, which are building blocks for keratin in hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/saw-palmetto

Saw palmetto is a palm native to the southeastern United States whose berries are sold as a dietary supplement. The article says it is commonly used in products for benign prostatic hyperplasia and scalp hair loss.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/horsetail-extract
Horsetail extract comes from the Equisetum arvense plant, best known for its high silica content. The article describes its composition, how it is used in hair care and its safety considerations.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/grape-seed-extract
Grape seed extract comes from the seeds of grapes, a byproduct of winemaking, and is rich in polyphenols, flavonoids and antioxidants. The article discusses how these compounds are used in hair care.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/flaxseed-oil

Flaxseed oil, also known as linseed oil, comes from the seeds of the flax plant, Linum usitatissimum. The article says it is rich in alpha-linolenic acid, an omega-3 fatty acid, and discusses its use for hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/tea-tree-oil

Tea tree oil, also called melaleuca oil, is an essential oil derived from the leaves of the Melaleuca alternifolia tree, native to Australia. The article says it is extracted by steam distillation and discusses its use for scalp care.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/msm-methylsulfonylmethane

MSM, or methylsulfonylmethane, is an organic sulfur-containing compound found naturally in plants, animals and humans. The article says its sulfur content is involved in making keratin and collagen, which are important for hair and skin.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/calcium

Calcium is a mineral known for bone and tooth health that also supports muscle function and nerve signaling. The article discusses its link to hair health, signs of low calcium, food sources and recommended daily intake.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/burdock-root
Burdock root is a vegetable that grows beneath the burdock plant and is known for its use in traditional medicine. The article describes its nutrients and how it is used for hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/bhringraj
Bhringraj is an herb long used in traditional Ayurvedic medicine, often called the king of herbs for hair care. The article says it contains compounds such as ecliptine, wedelolactone and coumestans.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/brahmi
Brahmi, or Bacopa monnieri, is a creeping herb long used in Ayurvedic medicine, also called the herb of grace. The article describes the plant and its potential use in hair care.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/jojoba-oil

Jojoba oil is extracted from the seeds of the jojoba plant, Simmondsia chinensis, and is technically a wax ester that resembles human sebum. The article says this makes it moisturizing and easily absorbed by the scalp and hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/argan-oil
Argan oil is a natural oil from the kernels of the argan tree, which is native to Morocco. The article says it is high in vitamin E and essential fatty acids and discusses its use for hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/coconut-oil
Coconut oil comes from the kernel of mature coconuts and is mostly saturated fats such as lauric acid. The article says these fats have an affinity for hair protein and enter the hair shaft.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/almond-oil
Almond oil is a natural oil from the kernels of sweet almonds, rich in vitamins E and A, omega-3 fatty acids and zinc. The article says it is used as a moisturizer and protectant for hair and skin.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/sunflower-oil

Sunflower oil is extracted from the seeds of the sunflower plant, Helianthus annuus, and is rich in vitamins, antioxidants and fatty acids. The article covers using it as a pre-shampoo oil, leave-in conditioner or in DIY masks.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/avocado-oil

Avocado oil is derived from the pulp of avocados and is rich in vitamins A, D, E and B-6, minerals such as magnesium and copper, and oleic acid. The article describes how these nutrients are used in hair care.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/black-seed-oil

Black seed oil is extracted from the seeds of the Nigella sativa plant and has a long history in traditional medicine. It contains antioxidants and thymoquinone, and the article describes how it is used in hair care.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/spirulina

Spirulina is a blue-green microalgae that grows in fresh and salt water. The article says it is rich in protein, B vitamins, minerals such as iron, magnesium and selenium, and antioxidants, and discusses its role in hair care.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/probiotics

Probiotics are live microorganisms, mainly bacteria, that provide a health benefit when consumed in adequate amounts. The article says they help maintain the gut microbiome and discusses the connection between gut health and hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/prebiotics

Prebiotics are non-digestible fibers that serve as food for beneficial gut bacteria. The article says they are found in fruits, vegetables and whole grains and explains the link between gut health and hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/beta-sitosterol

Beta-sitosterol is a plant sterol found in the cell membranes of fruits, vegetables, nuts and seeds, similar to cholesterol in humans. The article discusses its use as a supplement and its connection to hair thickness.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/ceramides

Ceramides are lipids found in high concentrations in the top layers of skin, including the scalp. The article says they form a protective barrier that locks in moisture and shields the skin from pollutants and irritants.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/quinoa-extract

Quinoa extract is derived from the quinoa plant, a grain crop with edible seeds that has been a staple in South America for thousands of years. The article says its protein and amino acid content is why it is used in hair care.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/tocotrienols

Tocotrienols are members of the vitamin E family, known for strong antioxidant properties. The article lists the four variants, alpha, beta, gamma and delta, and the foods they come from, including annatto seeds, palm oil and rice bran oil.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/baobab-oil
Baobab oil is a cold-pressed oil from the seeds of the baobab tree, which is native to the African savannahs. The article describes its nutrient profile and how it is used in hair care.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/sacha-inchi-oil

Sacha inchi oil comes from the seeds of the Plukenetia volubilis plant, native to South America's tropical rainforests. The article says it is high in omega-3, omega-6 and omega-9 fatty acids and vitamins A and E, and discusses its use for hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/sea-buckthorn-oil

Sea buckthorn oil is derived from the berries, seeds and leaves of the sea buckthorn shrub and has been used in traditional medicine for centuries. The article describes its nutritional profile and how it is used for dry, damaged hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/moringa-extract

Moringa extract comes from the leaves of the Moringa oleifera tree, which is native to parts of Africa and Asia. The article says the leaves contain vitamins A, C and E and discusses their use for hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/matcha-green-tea-extract

Matcha green tea extract is a concentrated form of green tea that contains vitamins A and C, zinc, selenium and the antioxidant EGCG. The article describes how these nutrients are used in hair and scalp care.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/hemp-seed-oil
Hemp seed oil comes from the seeds of the Cannabis sativa plant and does not contain THC. The article says it is rich in omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids and describes topical and oral use for hair.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/papaya-extract

Papaya extract is made from papaya and contains vitamins A and C, minerals and enzymes. The article says vitamin A is involved in sebum production and vitamin C in collagen synthesis, and discusses its use for dandruff and hair care.
/blogs/hair-vitamins/best-essential-oils
The article names lavender, rosemary and peppermint oil as the top essential oils for hair care. It advises diluting them with a carrier oil and doing a patch test before use.
/blogs/hair-care/how-to-use-fully-vital-hair-serums

The article explains how to apply a scalp hair serum: start with a clean scalp, fill the dropper, apply to thinning areas, massage in with your fingertips and leave it in overnight. It says the serum can also be used on non-wash days.
/blogs/hair-care/how-to-use-fully-vital-hair-supplements

The article explains how to take hair supplements: eat some healthy fats with your morning and evening meals. It says some ingredients in the supplements are water soluble and others are fat soluble, so fats help the nutrients absorb.
/blogs/hair-care/how-to-use-fully-vital-products

The article explains a daily routine that combines hair supplements taken each day with a scalp serum applied daily. It describes how to use each step so they fit together in one hair wellness routine.
/blogs/hair-care/glutathione-for-gray-hair

Hair color comes from melanocytes, which make the pigment melanin at the base of each follicle. The article explains how hydrogen peroxide builds up in aging follicles and how glutathione and catalase normally clear it.
